1	# Architecture Plan: Team Members + Candidate Notes + LinkedIn Button
2	
3	## 1. Key Architecture Decision: Teams Table vs Direct Linking
4	
5	**Decision: Use a `teams` table (workspace model).**
6	
7	Why not just `team_invitations` + `team_members` linking users directly?
8	
9	The direct-linking approach (owner_user_id + member_user_id) breaks down quickly:
10	- If the original user deletes their account, all team relationships are orphaned
11	- No clean place to store team-level settings (team name, shared credits, etc.)
12	- Upgrading to multi-team later requires a full schema rewrite
13	
14	The workspace model costs 2 extra tables now but saves a painful migration later. Every user who signs up gets an implicit personal team (auto-created in the `handle_new_user` trigger). When they invite someone, that person joins the existing team. Simple, extensible, and the RLS rewrite is straightforward.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 2. Complete SQL Migration
19	
20	```sql
21	-- ============================================================
22	-- MIGRATION: Team Members + Candidate Notes + LinkedIn Button
23	-- ============================================================
24	
25	-- ── 1. TEAM ROLE ENUM ─────────────────────────────────────────
26	CREATE TYPE public.team_role AS ENUM ('owner', 'admin', 'member');
27	
28	-- ── 2. TEAMS TABLE ────────────────────────────────────────────
29	-- Every user gets a personal team on signup. Teams own nothing
30	-- directly; they exist purely as a membership container.
31	-- Credits and billing stay on profiles (the owner's profile).
32	CREATE TABLE public.teams (
33	  id         uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
34	  name       text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'My Team',
35	  owner_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
36	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
37	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
38	);
39	
40	CREATE INDEX idx_teams_owner ON public.teams(owner_id);
41	
42	-- ── 3. TEAM MEMBERS TABLE ─────────────────────────────────────
43	-- Links users to teams with a role. Owner is auto-inserted.
44	-- A user can belong to multiple teams (their own + invited).
45	CREATE TABLE public.team_members (
46	  id        uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
47	  team_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
48	  user_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
49	  role      team_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
50	  joined_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
51	  UNIQUE(team_id, user_id)
52	);
53	
54	CREATE INDEX idx_team_members_team ON public.team_members(team_id);
55	CREATE INDEX idx_team_members_user ON public.team_members(user_id);
56	
57	-- ── 4. TEAM INVITATIONS TABLE ─────────────────────────────────
58	-- Pending invitations by email. When invited user signs up or
59	-- logs in, a trigger/check auto-accepts pending invitations.
60	CREATE TABLE public.team_invitations (
61	  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
62	  team_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
63	  email        text NOT NULL,
64	  role         team_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
65	  invited_by   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
66	  status       text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
67	                 CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'accepted', 'declined', 'expired')),
68	  token        text NOT NULL DEFAULT encode(gen_random_bytes(32), 'hex'),
69	  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
70	  expires_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT (now() + interval '7 days'),
71	  UNIQUE(team_id, email)
72	);
73	
74	CREATE INDEX idx_team_invitations_email ON public.team_invitations(email);
75	CREATE INDEX idx_team_invitations_team ON public.team_invitations(team_id);
76	CREATE INDEX idx_team_invitations_token ON public.team_invitations(token);
77	
78	-- ── 5. CANDIDATE NOTES TABLE ──────────────────────────────────
79	CREATE TABLE public.candidate_notes (
80	  id         uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
81	  resume_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
82	  job_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
83	  author_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
84	  note_type  text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'general'
85	               CHECK (note_type IN ('general', 'positive', 'concern', 'flag')),
86	  content    text NOT NULL,
87	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
88	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
89	);
90	
91	CREATE INDEX idx_candidate_notes_resume_job ON public.candidate_notes(resume_id, job_id);
92	CREATE INDEX idx_candidate_notes_job ON public.candidate_notes(job_id);
93	CREATE INDEX idx_candidate_notes_author ON public.candidate_notes(author_id);
94	
95	-- ── 6. ADD team_id TO JOBS TABLE ──────────────────────────────
96	-- Links jobs to a team so team members can access them.
97	-- Nullable initially; backfill sets it for existing jobs.
98	ALTER TABLE public.jobs ADD COLUMN team_id uuid REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
99	CREATE INDEX idx_jobs_team ON public.jobs(team_id);
100	
101	-- ── 7. HELPER FUNCTION: Check team membership ─────────────────
102	-- Returns true if user is a member of the team that owns a job.
103	-- Used in RLS policies across all job-scoped tables.
104	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_team_member_of_job(_user_id uuid, _job_id uuid)
105	RETURNS boolean
106	LANGUAGE sql
107	STABLE
108	SECURITY DEFINER
109	SET search_path = public
110	AS $$
111	  SELECT EXISTS (
112	    SELECT 1
113	    FROM public.jobs j
114	    JOIN public.team_members tm ON tm.team_id = j.team_id
115	    WHERE j.id = _job_id
116	      AND tm.user_id = _user_id
117	  )
118	$$;
119	
120	-- Also a direct team membership check
121	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_team_member(_user_id uuid, _team_id uuid)
122	RETURNS boolean
123	LANGUAGE sql
124	STABLE
125	SECURITY DEFINER
126	SET search_path = public
127	AS $$
128	  SELECT EXISTS (
129	    SELECT 1 FROM public.team_members
130	    WHERE team_id = _team_id AND user_id = _user_id
131	  )
132	$$;
133	
134	-- Check if user has admin+ role in a team
135	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_team_admin(_user_id uuid, _team_id uuid)
136	RETURNS boolean
137	LANGUAGE sql
138	STABLE
139	SECURITY DEFINER
140	SET search_path = public
141	AS $$
142	  SELECT EXISTS (
143	    SELECT 1 FROM public.team_members
144	    WHERE team_id = _team_id
145	      AND user_id = _user_id
146	      AND role IN ('owner', 'admin')
147	  )
148	$$;
149	
150	-- ── 8. AUTO-CREATE TEAM ON USER SIGNUP ────────────────────────
151	-- Modify existing handle_new_user to also create a personal team.
152	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()
153	RETURNS TRIGGER
154	LANGUAGE plpgsql
155	SECURITY DEFINER
156	SET search_path = public
157	AS $$
158	DECLARE
159	  new_team_id uuid;
160	BEGIN
161	  -- Create profile (existing behavior)
162	  INSERT INTO public.profiles (user_id, inbox_email)
163	  VALUES (NEW.id, encode(gen_random_bytes(8), 'hex') || '@inbound.rankora.co');
164	
165	  -- Create default user role (existing behavior)
166	  INSERT INTO public.user_roles (user_id, role) VALUES (NEW.id, 'user');
167	
168	  -- Create personal team
169	  INSERT INTO public.teams (name, owner_id)
170	  VALUES (
171	    COALESCE(
172	      NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name',
173	      split_part(NEW.email, '@', 1)
174	    ) || '''s Team',
175	    NEW.id
176	  )
177	  RETURNING id INTO new_team_id;
178	
179	  -- Add user as owner of their team
180	  INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
181	  VALUES (new_team_id, NEW.id, 'owner');
182	
183	  -- Auto-accept any pending invitations for this email
184	  -- (They signed up after being invited)
185	  INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
186	  SELECT ti.team_id, NEW.id, ti.role
187	  FROM public.team_invitations ti
188	  WHERE ti.email = NEW.email
189	    AND ti.status = 'pending'
190	    AND ti.expires_at > now()
191	  ON CONFLICT (team_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;
192	
193	  UPDATE public.team_invitations
194	  SET status = 'accepted'
195	  WHERE email = NEW.email AND status = 'pending';
196	
197	  RETURN NEW;
198	END;
199	$$;
200	
201	-- ── 9. BACKFILL: Create teams for existing users ──────────────
202	-- For every existing user without a team, create one and link their jobs.
203	DO $$
204	DECLARE
205	  r RECORD;
206	  new_team_id uuid;
207	BEGIN
208	  FOR r IN
209	    SELECT p.user_id, u.email, u.raw_user_meta_data
210	    FROM public.profiles p
211	    JOIN auth.users u ON u.id = p.user_id
212	    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
213	      SELECT 1 FROM public.team_members tm WHERE tm.user_id = p.user_id AND tm.role = 'owner'
214	    )
215	  LOOP
216	    INSERT INTO public.teams (name, owner_id)
217	    VALUES (
218	      COALESCE(
219	        r.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name',
220	        split_part(r.email, '@', 1)
221	      ) || '''s Team',
222	      r.user_id
223	    )
224	    RETURNING id INTO new_team_id;
225	
226	    INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
227	    VALUES (new_team_id, r.user_id, 'owner');
228	
229	    -- Link all existing jobs to this team
230	    UPDATE public.jobs SET team_id = new_team_id WHERE user_id = r.user_id;
231	  END LOOP;
232	END;
233	$$;
234	
235	-- ── 10. AUTO-SET team_id ON NEW JOBS ──────────────────────────
236	-- When a user creates a job, auto-fill team_id from their owned team.
237	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.auto_set_job_team_id()
238	RETURNS TRIGGER
239	LANGUAGE plpgsql
240	SECURITY DEFINER
241	SET search_path = public
242	AS $$
243	BEGIN
244	  IF NEW.team_id IS NULL THEN
245	    SELECT tm.team_id INTO NEW.team_id
246	    FROM public.team_members tm
247	    WHERE tm.user_id = NEW.user_id AND tm.role = 'owner'
248	    LIMIT 1;
249	  END IF;
250	  RETURN NEW;
251	END;
252	$$;
253	
254	CREATE TRIGGER set_job_team_id
255	  BEFORE INSERT ON public.jobs
256	  FOR EACH ROW
257	  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.auto_set_job_team_id();
258	
259	-- ── 11. RLS POLICIES ──────────────────────────────────────────
260	
261	-- --- Teams ---
262	ALTER TABLE public.teams ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
263	
264	CREATE POLICY "Members can view their teams"
265	  ON public.teams FOR SELECT TO authenticated
266	  USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), id));
267	
268	CREATE POLICY "Owner can update their team"
269	  ON public.teams FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
270	  USING (owner_id = auth.uid());
271	
272	-- Teams are created by trigger only
273	CREATE POLICY "No direct team insert"
274	  ON public.teams FOR INSERT TO authenticated
275	  WITH CHECK (false);
276	
277	-- --- Team Members ---
278	ALTER TABLE public.team_members ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
279	
280	CREATE POLICY "Members can view team roster"
281	  ON public.team_members FOR SELECT TO authenticated
282	  USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));
283	
284	-- Only team admins/owners can insert (invite acceptance is via trigger)
285	CREATE POLICY "Team admins can add members"
286	  ON public.team_members FOR INSERT TO authenticated
287	  WITH CHECK (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));
288	
289	-- Only team admins/owners can update roles
290	CREATE POLICY "Team admins can update member roles"
291	  ON public.team_members FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
292	  USING (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));
293	
294	-- Only team admins/owners can remove (or self-remove)
295	CREATE POLICY "Team admins can remove members"
296	  ON public.team_members FOR DELETE TO authenticated
297	  USING (
298	    public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id)
299	    OR user_id = auth.uid() -- members can leave
300	  );
301	
302	-- --- Team Invitations ---
303	ALTER TABLE public.team_invitations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

305	CREATE POLICY "Team admins can view invitations"

308	
309	CREATE POLICY "Team admins can create invitations"
310	  ON public.team_invitations FOR INSERT TO authenticated
311	  WITH CHECK (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));
312	
313	CREATE POLICY "Team admins can update invitations"
314	  ON public.team_invitations FOR UPDATE TO authenticated

348	-- Authors can delete their own notes; team admins can delete any

593	// src/lib/linkedin.ts
594	export function extractLinkedInUrl(result: Result): string | null {
595	  const pj = result.parsed_json;
596	  if (!pj) return null;
597	
598	  // Check common locations in parsed resume JSON
599	  if (typeof pj.linkedin === 'string' && pj.linkedin) return normalizeLinkedInUrl(pj.linkedin);
600	  if (pj.contact?.linkedin) return normalizeLinkedInUrl(pj.contact.linkedin);
601	  if (pj.links?.linkedin) return normalizeLinkedInUrl(pj.links.linkedin);
602	
603	  // Check applications table data (if merged into result)
604	  if ((result as any).linkedin_url) return normalizeLinkedInUrl((result as any).linkedin_url);
605	
606	  return null;
607	}
608	
609	function normalizeLinkedInUrl(url: string): string {
610	  if (url.startsWith('http')) return url;
611	  if (url.startsWith('linkedin.com') || url.startsWith('www.linkedin.com')) return 'https://' + url;
612	  // Handle bare profile IDs like "in/johndoe"
613	  if (url.startsWith('in/')) return 'https://www.linkedin.com/' + url;
614	  return 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/' + url;
615	}

762	
763	## 12. Risks and Mitigations
764	
765	| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
766	|------|-----------|--------|------------|
767	| RLS policy update breaks existing single-user queries | Medium | High | The new policies use OR logic: `user_id = auth.uid() OR team_member`. Existing users with no team_id on jobs still pass via `user_id = auth.uid()`. Backfill ensures all jobs get team_id. |
768	| `is_team_member_of_job` SECURITY DEFINER function has performance impact on large tables | Low | Medium | Function does a simple join on indexed columns (jobs.id, team_members.team_id, team_members.user_id). Acceptable for MVP scale. |
769	| Backfill fails for users with edge-case profiles | Low | Medium | Backfill is wrapped in a DO block with per-user iteration. If one user fails, others still process. Log and fix manually. |
770	| Invitation email spam | Low | Low | Rate limit invitations to 10 per team per day. Unique constraint on (team_id, email) prevents duplicate invites. |
771	| `handle_new_user` trigger becomes complex | Low | Medium | Now handles 3 responsibilities (profile, role, team). Still a single transaction. If team creation fails, the entire signup fails -- this is acceptable because the team is mandatory for the product to work. |
772	
773	---
774	
775	## 13. What is NOT in Scope (Deferred)
776	
777	- **Team-level billing / shared credits**: Credits stay on the owner's profile. Team members use the owner's credits when they process jobs. This is V2.
778	- **Multiple teams per user**: A user can technically belong to multiple teams (via invitations), but the UI only shows one active team. Multi-team switching is V2.
779	- **Granular permissions**: No per-job or per-feature permissions. Team roles (owner/admin/member) control everything. V2.
780	- **Team member job creation**: Only the job owner can create jobs. Team members can view and add notes but cannot create new jobs under the team. V2.
781	- **@mention notifications**: The content supports @mention syntax (text stored as-is), but no notification is sent. V2.
782	- **Note attachments**: Text only. No file attachments on notes. V2.
783	
784	---
785	
786	## 14. Technical Decisions Summary
787	
788	| Decision | Choice | Reasoning |
789	|----------|--------|-----------|
790	| Team model | Dedicated `teams` table | Extensible for multi-team, team settings, team billing in V2. Direct user-linking would need a rewrite later. |
791	| Team creation | Auto on signup via trigger | Every user always has a team. No "create team" flow needed. Simpler UX. |
792	| Job scoping | `team_id` column on `jobs` | Clean FK relationship. Backfill is simple. Auto-set via trigger on insert. |
793	| RLS approach | OR-based policies | `user_id = auth.uid() OR is_team_member(...)`. Backwards compatible -- solo users unaffected. |
794	| Team member permissions | Read-only for `member` role | MVP simplicity. Members can view everything + add notes. Only owner/admin can modify jobs/stages. |
795	| Notes location | Inside CandidateDetailSheet | Notes are contextual to a specific candidate evaluation. Not a standalone page. |
796	| LinkedIn URL | Extract from existing `parsed_json` | No new data needed. GPT-4o already extracts LinkedIn URLs during resume parsing when available. |
797	| Realtime for notes | Supabase realtime subscription | Team members see each other's notes instantly without polling. Already have the pattern from feature_flags. |
798	| Invite acceptance | Trigger-based for new users, edge function for existing | New users auto-join via `handle_new_user`. Existing users need explicit acceptance (security: don't auto-add existing users to teams without consent). |

# Architecture Plan: Team Members + Candidate Notes + LinkedIn Button

## 1. Key Architecture Decision: Teams Table vs Direct Linking

**Decision: Use a `teams` table (workspace model).**

Why not just `team_invitations` + `team_members` linking users directly?

The direct-linking approach (owner_user_id + member_user_id) breaks down quickly:
- If the original user deletes their account, all team relationships are orphaned
- No clean place to store team-level settings (team name, shared credits, etc.)
- Upgrading to multi-team later requires a full schema rewrite

The workspace model costs 2 extra tables now but saves a painful migration later. Every user who signs up gets an implicit personal team (auto-created in the `handle_new_user` trigger). When they invite someone, that person joins the existing team. Simple, extensible, and the RLS rewrite is straightforward.

---

## 2. Complete SQL Migration

```sql
-- ============================================================
-- MIGRATION: Team Members + Candidate Notes + LinkedIn Button
-- ============================================================

-- ── 1. TEAM ROLE ENUM ─────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TYPE public.team_role AS ENUM ('owner', 'admin', 'member');

-- ── 2. TEAMS TABLE ────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Every user gets a personal team on signup. Teams own nothing
-- directly; they exist purely as a membership container.
-- Credits and billing stay on profiles (the owner's profile).
CREATE TABLE public.teams (
  id         uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name       text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'My Team',
  owner_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_teams_owner ON public.teams(owner_id);

-- ── 3. TEAM MEMBERS TABLE ─────────────────────────────────────
-- Links users to teams with a role. Owner is auto-inserted.
-- A user can belong to multiple teams (their own + invited).
CREATE TABLE public.team_members (
  id        uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role      team_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
  joined_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE(team_id, user_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_team_members_team ON public.team_members(team_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_team_members_user ON public.team_members(user_id);

-- ── 4. TEAM INVITATIONS TABLE ─────────────────────────────────
-- Pending invitations by email. When invited user signs up or
-- logs in, a trigger/check auto-accepts pending invitations.
CREATE TABLE public.team_invitations (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  email        text NOT NULL,
  role         team_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
  invited_by   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  status       text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
                 CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'accepted', 'declined', 'expired')),
  token        text NOT NULL DEFAULT encode(gen_random_bytes(32), 'hex'),
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT (now() + interval '7 days'),
  UNIQUE(team_id, email)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_team_invitations_email ON public.team_invitations(email);
CREATE INDEX idx_team_invitations_team ON public.team_invitations(team_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_team_invitations_token ON public.team_invitations(token);

-- ── 5. CANDIDATE NOTES TABLE ──────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE public.candidate_notes (
  id         uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  resume_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.resumes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id     uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  author_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  note_type  text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'general'
               CHECK (note_type IN ('general', 'positive', 'concern', 'flag')),
  content    text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_candidate_notes_resume_job ON public.candidate_notes(resume_id, job_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_candidate_notes_job ON public.candidate_notes(job_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_candidate_notes_author ON public.candidate_notes(author_id);

-- ── 6. ADD team_id TO JOBS TABLE ──────────────────────────────
-- Links jobs to a team so team members can access them.
-- Nullable initially; backfill sets it for existing jobs.
ALTER TABLE public.jobs ADD COLUMN team_id uuid REFERENCES public.teams(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_jobs_team ON public.jobs(team_id);

-- ── 7. HELPER FUNCTION: Check team membership ─────────────────
-- Returns true if user is a member of the team that owns a job.
-- Used in RLS policies across all job-scoped tables.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_team_member_of_job(_user_id uuid, _job_id uuid)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM public.jobs j
    JOIN public.team_members tm ON tm.team_id = j.team_id
    WHERE j.id = _job_id
      AND tm.user_id = _user_id
  )
$$;

-- Also a direct team membership check
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_team_member(_user_id uuid, _team_id uuid)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.team_members
    WHERE team_id = _team_id AND user_id = _user_id
  )
$$;

-- Check if user has admin+ role in a team
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_team_admin(_user_id uuid, _team_id uuid)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.team_members
    WHERE team_id = _team_id
      AND user_id = _user_id
      AND role IN ('owner', 'admin')
  )
$$;

-- ── 8. AUTO-CREATE TEAM ON USER SIGNUP ────────────────────────
-- Modify existing handle_new_user to also create a personal team.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  new_team_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Create profile (existing behavior)
  INSERT INTO public.profiles (user_id, inbox_email)
  VALUES (NEW.id, encode(gen_random_bytes(8), 'hex') || '@inbound.rankora.co');

  -- Create default user role (existing behavior)
  INSERT INTO public.user_roles (user_id, role) VALUES (NEW.id, 'user');

  -- Create personal team
  INSERT INTO public.teams (name, owner_id)
  VALUES (
    COALESCE(
      NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name',
      split_part(NEW.email, '@', 1)
    ) || '''s Team',
    NEW.id
  )
  RETURNING id INTO new_team_id;

  -- Add user as owner of their team
  INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
  VALUES (new_team_id, NEW.id, 'owner');

  -- Auto-accept any pending invitations for this email
  -- (They signed up after being invited)
  INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
  SELECT ti.team_id, NEW.id, ti.role
  FROM public.team_invitations ti
  WHERE ti.email = NEW.email
    AND ti.status = 'pending'
    AND ti.expires_at > now()
  ON CONFLICT (team_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;

  UPDATE public.team_invitations
  SET status = 'accepted'
  WHERE email = NEW.email AND status = 'pending';

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

-- ── 9. BACKFILL: Create teams for existing users ──────────────
-- For every existing user without a team, create one and link their jobs.
DO $$
DECLARE
  r RECORD;
  new_team_id uuid;
BEGIN
  FOR r IN
    SELECT p.user_id, u.email, u.raw_user_meta_data
    FROM public.profiles p
    JOIN auth.users u ON u.id = p.user_id
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.team_members tm WHERE tm.user_id = p.user_id AND tm.role = 'owner'
    )
  LOOP
    INSERT INTO public.teams (name, owner_id)
    VALUES (
      COALESCE(
        r.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name',
        split_part(r.email, '@', 1)
      ) || '''s Team',
      r.user_id
    )
    RETURNING id INTO new_team_id;

    INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role)
    VALUES (new_team_id, r.user_id, 'owner');

    -- Link all existing jobs to this team
    UPDATE public.jobs SET team_id = new_team_id WHERE user_id = r.user_id;
  END LOOP;
END;
$$;

-- ── 10. AUTO-SET team_id ON NEW JOBS ──────────────────────────
-- When a user creates a job, auto-fill team_id from their owned team.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.auto_set_job_team_id()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.team_id IS NULL THEN
    SELECT tm.team_id INTO NEW.team_id
    FROM public.team_members tm
    WHERE tm.user_id = NEW.user_id AND tm.role = 'owner'
    LIMIT 1;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER set_job_team_id
  BEFORE INSERT ON public.jobs
  FOR EACH ROW
  EXECUTE FUNCTION public.auto_set_job_team_id();

-- ── 11. RLS POLICIES ──────────────────────────────────────────

-- --- Teams ---
ALTER TABLE public.teams ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "Members can view their teams"
  ON public.teams FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), id));

CREATE POLICY "Owner can update their team"
  ON public.teams FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
  USING (owner_id = auth.uid());

-- Teams are created by trigger only
CREATE POLICY "No direct team insert"
  ON public.teams FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (false);

-- --- Team Members ---
ALTER TABLE public.team_members ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "Members can view team roster"
  ON public.team_members FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Only team admins/owners can insert (invite acceptance is via trigger)
CREATE POLICY "Team admins can add members"
  ON public.team_members FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Only team admins/owners can update roles
CREATE POLICY "Team admins can update member roles"
  ON public.team_members FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
  USING (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Only team admins/owners can remove (or self-remove)
CREATE POLICY "Team admins can remove members"
  ON public.team_members FOR DELETE TO authenticated
  USING (
    public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id)
    OR user_id = auth.uid() -- members can leave
  );

-- --- Team Invitations ---
ALTER TABLE public.team_invitations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "Team admins can view invitations"
  ON public.team_invitations FOR SELECT TO authenticated

  ON public.team_invitations FOR INSERT TO authenticated

  ON public.team_invitations FOR UPDATE TO authenticated

CREATE POLICY "Team admins can delete invitations"
  ON public.team_invitations FOR DELETE TO authenticated

-- --- Candidate Notes ---

-- Team members can view notes on jobs they have access to
CREATE POLICY "Team members can view notes"

    public.is_job_owner(auth.uid(), job_id)
    OR public.is_team_member_of_job(auth.uid(), job_id)

-- Any team member can add notes
CREATE POLICY "Team members can add notes"
  ON public.candidate_notes FOR INSERT TO authenticated

    author_id = auth.uid()
    AND (
      public.is_job_owner(auth.uid(), job_id)
      OR public.is_team_member_of_job(auth.uid(), job_id)
    )
  );

-- Authors can edit their own notes
CREATE POLICY "Authors can update own notes"
  ON public.candidate_notes FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
  USING (author_id = auth.uid());

-- Authors can delete their own notes; team admins can delete any
CREATE POLICY "Authors and admins can delete notes"
  ON public.candidate_notes FOR DELETE TO authenticated
  USING (
    author_id = auth.uid()
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.jobs j
      JOIN public.team_members tm ON tm.team_id = j.team_id
      WHERE j.id = candidate_notes.job_id
        AND tm.user_id = auth.uid()
        AND tm.role IN ('owner', 'admin')
    )
  );

-- ── 12. UPDATE EXISTING JOB RLS POLICIES ──────────────────────
-- Team members need to see jobs owned by their team.
-- We DROP and recreate the job SELECT policy.

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users read own jobs" ON public.jobs;
CREATE POLICY "Users read own or team jobs" ON public.jobs
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    user_id = auth.uid()
    OR (team_id IS NOT NULL AND public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id))
  );

-- Keep insert/update/delete restricted to job owner only
-- (team members can view but not modify jobs for MVP)

-- ── 13. UPDATE EXISTING RESUMES RLS ───────────────────────────
-- Team members need to see resumes for team jobs.

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users read own resumes" ON public.resumes;
CREATE POLICY "Users read own or team resumes" ON public.resumes
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    public.is_job_owner(auth.uid(), job_id)
    OR public.is_team_member_of_job(auth.uid(), job_id)
  );

-- ── 14. UPDATE EXISTING RESULTS RLS ──────────────────────────
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users read own results" ON public.results;
CREATE POLICY "Users read own or team results" ON public.results
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.resumes r
      JOIN public.jobs j ON r.job_id = j.id
      WHERE r.id = results.resume_id
        AND (
          j.user_id = auth.uid()
          OR (j.team_id IS NOT NULL AND public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), j.team_id))
        )
    )
  );

-- ── 15. UPDATE CANDIDATE_STAGES RLS ──────────────────────────
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can view stages for own jobs" ON public.candidate_stages;
CREATE POLICY "Users can view stages for own or team jobs" ON public.candidate_stages
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.jobs WHERE jobs.id = candidate_stages.job_id AND jobs.user_id = auth.uid())
    OR public.is_team_member_of_job(auth.uid(), job_id)
  );

-- Members with 'member' role can only view, not modify stages
-- (owner and admin keep existing insert/update/delete policies)

-- ── 16. UPDATE STAGE_HISTORY RLS ─────────────────────────────
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can view stage history for own jobs" ON public.stage_history;
CREATE POLICY "Users can view stage history for own or team jobs" ON public.stage_history
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.jobs WHERE jobs.id = stage_history.job_id AND jobs.user_id = auth.uid())
    OR public.is_team_member_of_job(auth.uid(), job_id)
  );

-- ── 17. UPDATE APPLICATIONS RLS ──────────────────────────────
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "applications_owner_select" ON public.applications;
CREATE POLICY "applications_owner_or_team_select" ON public.applications
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM jobs
      WHERE jobs.id = applications.job_id
        AND (
          jobs.user_id = auth.uid()
          OR (jobs.team_id IS NOT NULL AND public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), jobs.team_id))
        )
    )
  );

-- ── 18. TRIGGERS ──────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TRIGGER update_teams_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.teams
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column();

CREATE TRIGGER update_candidate_notes_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.candidate_notes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column();

-- ── 19. ENABLE REALTIME ───────────────────────────────────────
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE public.candidate_notes;

-- ── 20. COMMENTS ──────────────────────────────────────────────
COMMENT ON TABLE public.teams IS 'Workspace container; every user auto-gets a personal team';
COMMENT ON TABLE public.team_members IS 'Links users to teams with role (owner/admin/member)';
COMMENT ON TABLE public.team_invitations IS 'Pending email invitations to join a team';
COMMENT ON TABLE public.candidate_notes IS 'Collaborative notes on candidates, scoped to resume+job';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.jobs.team_id IS 'Team that owns this job; auto-set from creator on insert';
```

## 3. RLS Data Flow Diagram

Current RLS chain (single user):
```
auth.uid() = jobs.user_id  -->  resumes via is_job_owner  -->  results via resume->job->user_id
```

New RLS chain (team-aware):
```
auth.uid() = jobs.user_id                           (owner: full CRUD)
  OR
auth.uid() IN team_members WHERE team_id = jobs.team_id  (member: SELECT only)
  |
  +--> resumes: SELECT if is_job_owner OR is_team_member_of_job
  +--> results: SELECT if job owner OR team member
  +--> candidate_stages: SELECT if job owner OR team member (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE: owner only)
  +--> candidate_notes: SELECT/INSERT if team member; UPDATE/DELETE own notes only
  +--> applications: SELECT if job owner OR team member
```

Key principle: **Team members get read access to everything in the team's jobs. Only the job owner retains write access to jobs, resumes, results, and stages. Notes are the one exception -- all team members can create notes, but can only edit/delete their own.**

```ts
// src/lib/linkedin.ts
export function extractLinkedInUrl(result: Result): string | null {
  const pj = result.parsed_json;
  if (!pj) return null;

  // Check common locations in parsed resume JSON
  if (typeof pj.linkedin === 'string' && pj.linkedin) return normalizeLinkedInUrl(pj.linkedin);
  if (pj.contact?.linkedin) return normalizeLinkedInUrl(pj.contact.linkedin);
  if (pj.links?.linkedin) return normalizeLinkedInUrl(pj.links.linkedin);

  // Check applications table data (if merged into result)
  if ((result as any).linkedin_url) return normalizeLinkedInUrl((result as any).linkedin_url);

  return null;
}

function normalizeLinkedInUrl(url: string): string {
  if (url.startsWith('http')) return url;
  if (url.startsWith('linkedin.com') || url.startsWith('www.linkedin.com')) return 'https://' + url;
  // Handle bare profile IDs like "in/johndoe"
  if (url.startsWith('in/')) return 'https://www.linkedin.com/' + url;
  return 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/' + url;
}
```

## 7. Data Flow: Team Membership Check

```
1. User logs in
2. useAuth fetches profile (existing)
3. NEW: useTeam hook fetches user's teams:
     SELECT t.*, tm.role
     FROM team_members tm
     JOIN teams t ON t.id = tm.team_id
     WHERE tm.user_id = auth.uid()
4. Store in TeamContext: { teams, activeTeam, activeRole }
5. For MVP, activeTeam = the team where role = 'owner'
```

### Invite Flow

```
1. Owner/Admin enters email on /team page
2. INSERT into team_invitations (email, role, team_id, invited_by)
3. Call send-email edge function to send invite email with link
4. Link format: https://rankora.co/auth?invite=<token>
5. When invitee visits link:
   a. If already has account: POST to accept-invitation edge function
      -> Validates token, inserts team_member, updates invitation status
   b. If new user: signs up normally
      -> handle_new_user trigger auto-accepts pending invitations for that email
6. React Query invalidates team_members query
```

### Accepting Invitation (existing user)

```
1. User clicks invite link -> /auth?invite=<token>
2. After login, check for `invite` search param
3. Call accept-invitation edge function:
   - Validate token exists, not expired, status = 'pending'
   - Insert into team_members
   - Update invitation status to 'accepted'
4. Redirect to /team showing new team membership
```

## 12. Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| RLS policy update breaks existing single-user queries | Medium | High | The new policies use OR logic: `user_id = auth.uid() OR team_member`. Existing users with no team_id on jobs still pass via `user_id = auth.uid()`. Backfill ensures all jobs get team_id. |
| `is_team_member_of_job` SECURITY DEFINER function has performance impact on large tables | Low | Medium | Function does a simple join on indexed columns (jobs.id, team_members.team_id, team_members.user_id). Acceptable for MVP scale. |
| Backfill fails for users with edge-case profiles | Low | Medium | Backfill is wrapped in a DO block with per-user iteration. If one user fails, others still process. Log and fix manually. |
| Invitation email spam | Low | Low | Rate limit invitations to 10 per team per day. Unique constraint on (team_id, email) prevents duplicate invites. |
| `handle_new_user` trigger becomes complex | Low | Medium | Now handles 3 responsibilities (profile, role, team). Still a single transaction. If team creation fails, the entire signup fails -- this is acceptable because the team is mandatory for the product to work. |

---

## 13. What is NOT in Scope (Deferred)

- **Team-level billing / shared credits**: Credits stay on the owner's profile. Team members use the owner's credits when they process jobs. This is V2.
- **Multiple teams per user**: A user can technically belong to multiple teams (via invitations), but the UI only shows one active team. Multi-team switching is V2.
- **Granular permissions**: No per-job or per-feature permissions. Team roles (owner/admin/member) control everything. V2.
- **Team member job creation**: Only the job owner can create jobs. Team members can view and add notes but cannot create new jobs under the team. V2.
- **@mention notifications**: The content supports @mention syntax (text stored as-is), but no notification is sent. V2.
- **Note attachments**: Text only. No file attachments on notes. V2.

---

## 14. Technical Decisions Summary

| Decision | Choice | Reasoning |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Team model | Dedicated `teams` table | Extensible for multi-team, team settings, team billing in V2. Direct user-linking would need a rewrite later. |
| Team creation | Auto on signup via trigger | Every user always has a team. No "create team" flow needed. Simpler UX. |
| Job scoping | `team_id` column on `jobs` | Clean FK relationship. Backfill is simple. Auto-set via trigger on insert. |
| RLS approach | OR-based policies | `user_id = auth.uid() OR is_team_member(...)`. Backwards compatible -- solo users unaffected. |
| Team member permissions | Read-only for `member` role | MVP simplicity. Members can view everything + add notes. Only owner/admin can modify jobs/stages. |
| Notes location | Inside CandidateDetailSheet | Notes are contextual to a specific candidate evaluation. Not a standalone page. |
| LinkedIn URL | Extract from existing `parsed_json` | No new data needed. GPT-4o already extracts LinkedIn URLs during resume parsing when available. |
| Realtime for notes | Supabase realtime subscription | Team members see each other's notes instantly without polling. Already have the pattern from feature_flags. |
| Invite acceptance | Trigger-based for new users, edge function for existing | New users auto-join via `handle_new_user`. Existing users need explicit acceptance (security: don't auto-add existing users to teams without consent). |

All 7 tasks done. Build passes clean. Here's the complete summary:

## What Was Built

### Section 1: Apply Connect (already done last session)
Already pushed — apply page, edge function, realtime, count badge.

### Section 2: Team Collaboration (MVP)

| Component | File | What It Does |
|---|---|---|
| **DB Migration** | `supabase/migrations/20260407100000_add_teams_and_notes.sql` | 4 new tables (teams, team_members, team_invitations, candidate_notes), RLS policies, auto-team on signup, backfill existing users, team-aware job/resume/results access |
| **Send Invite** | `supabase/functions/send-team-invite/index.ts` | Edge function: validates admin, creates invitation, sends email via Resend |
| **Accept Invite** | `supabase/functions/accept-team-invite/index.ts` | Edge function: validates token, adds member, handles new/existing users |
| **useTeam Hook** | `src/hooks/useTeam.tsx` | Fetches team, members, invitations via React Query |
| **Team Page** | `src/pages/Team.tsx` | Full page: invite form + pending invitations + members table with role management |
| **Sidebar** | `src/components/JobSidebar.tsx` | Added "Team" nav item with Users icon |
| **Route** | `src/App.tsx` | Added `/team` protected route |

### Section 3: LinkedIn Profile Button

| Component | File | What It Does |
|---|---|---|
| **URL Extractor** | `src/lib/linkedin.ts` | Extracts LinkedIn URL from parsed_json or applications data |
| **Detail Sheet** | `src/components/CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` | Blue "LinkedIn" button in action bar (shows only when URL found) |
| **Candidate Row** | `src/components/CandidateRow.tsx` | LinkedIn icon in row actions (hover blue #0A66C2) |

### Candidate Notes

| Component | File | What It Does |
|---|---|---|
| **Notes Hook** | `src/hooks/useCandidateNotes.tsx` | CRUD + realtime subscription for notes |
| **Notes Panel** | `src/components/candidate/CandidateNotesPanel.tsx` | Notes list + add form with type tags (General/Positive/Concern/Flag) |
| **Integration** | `src/components/CandidateDetailSheet.tsx` | Panel added between StageTracker and JD analysis |

### New Sidebar Navigation
```
Dashboard
My Jobs
Billing
Settings
Team          ← NEW
[New Job button]
```

Now let me generate the final comprehensive audit report:

## COMPREHENSIVE AUDIT REPORT
**Rankora: Team Collaboration, Candidate Notes & LinkedIn Features**
April 5, 2026

---

## CRITICAL ISSUES FOUND

### 1. **CRITICAL: Team.tsx Invite Flow Bypasses Edge Function - No Email Sent**
**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/pages/Team.tsx` (Lines 109-137)  
**Severity:** CRITICAL  
**Issue:**
The `handleInvite()` function performs a **direct database insert** instead of calling the `send-team-invite` edge function. This means:
- Emails are NEVER sent to invited users
- The invitation token is NOT generated
- Users cannot accept invitations because they never receive them

**Current code (WRONG):**
```typescript
const { error } = await (supabase as any)
  .from("team_invitations")
  .insert({
    team_id: team?.id,
    email: inviteEmail.trim().toLowerCase(),
    role: inviteRole,
    invited_by: user?.id,
    status: "pending",
    expires_at: new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
  });
```

**Expected code (CORRECT):**
```typescript
const { error } = await fetch(
  `${import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/send-team-invite`,
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "Authorization": `Bearer ${(await supabase.auth.getSession())?.data.session?.access_token}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      team_id: team?.id,
      email: inviteEmail.trim().toLowerCase(),
      role: inviteRole,
    }),
  }
).then(r => r.json());
```

**Fix:** Replace direct insert with edge function call to `send-team-invite`. This function handles email sending, token generation, and duplicate prevention.

---

### 2. **CRITICAL: useTeam Hook Only Fetches Owner's Team - Non-Owners Can't Access**
**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/hooks/useTeam.tsx` (Lines 40-46)  
**Severity:** CRITICAL  
**Issue:**
The query filters by `role = 'owner'`, meaning:
- Team members with 'admin' or 'member' roles visiting `/team` will get `team: null`
- Non-owners see empty team, empty members list, empty invitations
- RLS prevents non-owners from seeing their team data

**Current code (WRONG):**
```typescript
const { data: tmData } = await (supabase as any)
  .from("team_members")
  .select("team_id, role")
  .eq("user_id", userId)
  .eq("role", "owner")  // <-- ONLY owners
  .limit(1)
  .maybeSingle();

if (!tmData?.team_id) return { team: null, members: [], invitations: [], myRole: null };
```

**Expected behavior:** Fetch ANY team the user is a member of (owner, admin, or member role):
```typescript
const { data: tmData } = await (supabase as any)
  .from("team_members")
  .select("team_id, role")
  .eq("user_id", userId)
  .limit(1)
  .maybeSingle();
```

**Additional Issue:** The RLS policy on `team_invitations` restricts to team admins:

### 9. **MEDIUM: send-team-invite Function Missing Error Case**
**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/functions/send-team-invite/index.ts` (Lines 237-248)  
**Severity:** MEDIUM  
**Issue:**
When checking if a user is already a member (lines 238-248), the code calls `listUsers()` without pagination:
```typescript
await supabase.auth.admin.listUsers().then(({ data }) =>
  data?.users?.find((u) => u.email?.toLowerCase() === normalizedEmail)?.id || ""
)
```

**Problem:**
- `listUsers()` has a default page size (typically 50)
- If the invited user exists but is beyond page 50, they won't be found
- Function might create duplicate invitation or fail silently

**Fix:** Add pagination loop or use a better approach:
```typescript
// Try to find user by email using auth.admin.getUserByEmail if available
// Or fetch all pages with pagination
```

### 10. **MEDIUM: accept-team-invite RLS Context**
**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/functions/accept-team-invite/index.ts` (Lines 165-180)  
**Severity:** MEDIUM  
**Issue:**
The function inserts into `team_members` using the service role client (bypasses RLS), but the RLS policy requires `is_team_admin()`:
```sql
CREATE POLICY "Team admins can add members"
  ON public.team_members FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id));
```

This is fine because service role bypasses RLS. However, if the code is ever refactored to use authenticated client, it will fail. The comment on line 45 acknowledges this:
```typescript
// Service role client — needed to bypass RLS for reading/updating invitations
```

**Risk:** Low (intentional design), but should document why service role is needed.

Table creation uses ON DELETE CASCADE for foreign keys, which is good. However:
- Deleting a team cascades to team_members, team_invitations, candidate_notes
- Deleting a job cascades to candidate_notes ✓
- Deleting a user cascades to teams (which cascades to everything)

This is correct and matches the intended behavior. No issue here.

### 12. **LOW: Unused Email Config in send-team-invite**
**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/functions/send-team-invite/index.ts` (Lines 328-367)  
**Severity:** LOW  
**Issue:**
The function loads email config from `platform_config` table:
```typescript
const { data: emailConfig } = await supabase
  .from("platform_config")
  .select("resend_api_key, email_from_address, email_from_name, outbound_email_enabled")
  .limit(1)
  .single();
```

This is good for flexibility, but if the table has no rows or the query fails silently (error not thrown), the function uses fallbacks. The function continues even if email sending fails (lines 353-364).

**Risk:** Low — email is best-effort, invitation is still created. Users can manually resend if needed.

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/candidate/CandidateNotesPanel.tsx` (Lines 50-57, 86-87)

The `getInitials()` function tries to extract initials from email:

```typescript
const getInitials = (authorId: string) => {
  if (authorId === user?.id) return "You";
```

```typescript
  .from("candidate_notes")
  .select("*, profiles(full_name, email)")
  .eq("resume_id", resumeId)
  .eq("job_id", jobId);
```

Then update getInitials to use real name.

Based on my thorough exploration of the Rankora codebase, here's my complete analysis for planning the Tasks and Team Notifications features:

## FINDINGS SUMMARY

### Current Notifications System

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/NotificationBell.tsx` (Lines 1-200)
**Schema:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260331000000_add_notifications.sql` (Lines 1-42)

**Current Notification Types (CHECK constraint):**
```sql
check (type in ('ranking_complete', 'ranking_failed', 'credits_low', 'credits_added', 'system'))
```

**UI Implementation:**
- NotificationBell uses type-based icon mapping (ICON_MAP) with 5 types
- Real-time subscription via Postgres changes (INSERT events filtered by user_id)
- Supports metadata field (jsonb) for extensibility
- Unread badge with count up to 99+
- "Mark all read" functionality
- 20-notification limit in fetch, full payload persists

**RLS Policies:**
- Users can only view/update their own notifications
- Service role can insert (for edge functions)

**Key Insight:** Notifications are user-scoped, not team-scoped. Current schema is single-user model.

---

### Team System Architecture

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260407100000_add_teams_and_notes.sql` (Lines 1-502)

**Team Structure:**
```
teams (id, name, owner_id, created_at, updated_at)
team_members (id, team_id, user_id, role, joined_at)
  - Roles: 'owner', 'admin', 'member'
  - UNIQUE(team_id, user_id)
team_invitations (id, team_id, email, role, invited_by, status, token, created_at, expires_at)
  - Status: 'pending' | 'accepted' | 'declined' | 'expired'
candidate_notes (id, resume_id, job_id, author_id, note_type, content, created_at, updated_at)
  - note_type: 'general' | 'positive' | 'concern' | 'flag'
```

**Jobs Integration:**
- `jobs` table has `team_id` column (nullable, set via trigger `auto_set_job_team_id`)
- New jobs auto-assign to user's owner team
- Backfill updated all existing jobs to team_id of owner's personal team

**Helper Functions (Lines 94-128):**
- `is_team_member(_user_id uuid, _team_id uuid)` — returns boolean
- `is_team_admin(_user_id uuid, _team_id uuid)` — owner/admin check
- `is_team_member_of_job(_user_id uuid, _job_id uuid)` — checks if user is member of job's team

**User Hook:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/hooks/useTeam.tsx` (Lines 30-86)
- Returns: `team`, `members`, `invitations`, `myRole`, `isLoading`, `refetch`
- Prefers user's owner team, falls back to first team membership
- Stale time: 60 seconds

---

### Stage Tracking System

**Files:**
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/hooks/useStageTracker.ts` (Lines 1-137)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/candidate/StageTracker.tsx` (Lines 1-100+)

**Stage Types:**
```typescript
type HiringStage = "applied" | "screened" | "interview" | "offer" | "hired" | "rejected";
```

**Stage Change Flow:**
1. `useUpdateStage()` mutation upserts to `candidate_stages` table
2. Automatically logs to `stage_history` table (via insert in hook)
3. Triggers `onSuccess` toast: "Stage updated"
4. Invalidates react-query cache for that job's stages
5. **No notification currently created on stage change**

**Database Tables:**
```
candidate_stages (id, resume_id, job_id, stage, updated_at, updated_by)
  - Key for upsert: (resume_id, job_id)
stage_history (id, resume_id, job_id, from_stage, to_stage, changed_by, created_at)
  - Logs all transitions (non-critical, no error blocking)
```

---

### Existing Patterns Reference

**Candidate Notes Pattern:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/candidate/CandidateNotesPanel.tsx` (Lines 1-150+)
- Form with textarea + note_type selector (general/positive/concern/flag)
- Real-time subscription per resume_id
- Delete only by author or team admins

Completing Section 2 of the Rankora roadmap. Team Members + Notes are built. Now adding Tasks (assign work to teammates with due dates) and Team Notifications (stage changes, new notes, task assignments show in notification bell).

## Part 1: Tasks

### New Migration: `supabase/migrations/20260407200000_add_tasks_and_team_notifications.sql`

**Tasks table:**
```sql
CREATE TABLE public.tasks (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title text NOT NULL,
  description text,
  assigned_to uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id uuid REFERENCES jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  resume_id uuid REFERENCES resumes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo' CHECK (status IN ('todo', 'in_progress', 'done')),
  priority text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium' CHECK (priority IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')),
  due_date date,
  completed_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

**RLS:** Team members can SELECT. Owner/admin/creator can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Assigned user can UPDATE status.

**Extend notifications CHECK constraint:**
```sql
ALTER TABLE notifications DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS notifications_type_check;
ALTER TABLE notifications ADD CONSTRAINT notifications_type_check
  CHECK (type IN ('ranking_complete','ranking_failed','credits_low','credits_added','system',
                  'stage_changed','note_added','task_assigned','task_completed','member_joined'));
```

- `stage_history` INSERT → notify all team members of that job (except actor)
- `candidate_notes` INSERT → notify team members (except author)
- `tasks` INSERT (when assigned_to is set) → notify assigned user

## Section 2: RLS for Tasks

```sql
ALTER TABLE public.tasks ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Team members can view all tasks in their team
CREATE POLICY "Team members can view tasks"
  ON public.tasks FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id));

-- Team owner/admin/creator can insert tasks
CREATE POLICY "Team members can create tasks"
  ON public.tasks FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (
    created_by = auth.uid()
    AND public.is_team_member(auth.uid(), team_id)
  );

-- Creator, assigned user, or team admin can update
CREATE POLICY "Task participants can update"
  ON public.tasks FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
  USING (
    created_by = auth.uid()
    OR assigned_to = auth.uid()
    OR public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id)
  );

-- Creator or team admin can delete
CREATE POLICY "Task owners can delete"
  ON public.tasks FOR DELETE TO authenticated
  USING (
    created_by = auth.uid()
    OR public.is_team_admin(auth.uid(), team_id)
  );
```

## Section 4: DB Triggers for Auto-Notifications

### 4a. Task Assignment Notification
When a task is created with `assigned_to` set, or when `assigned_to` is updated to a new user, notify the assigned user:
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.notify_task_assigned()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Only notify if assigned to someone other than creator
  IF NEW.assigned_to IS NOT NULL AND NEW.assigned_to != NEW.created_by THEN
    -- For INSERT: always notify
    -- For UPDATE: only if assigned_to changed
    IF (TG_OP = 'INSERT') OR (TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.assigned_to IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.assigned_to) THEN
      INSERT INTO public.notifications (user_id, type, title, message, metadata)
      VALUES (
        NEW.assigned_to,
        'task_assigned',
        'New task assigned',
        'You''ve been assigned: ' || LEFT(NEW.title, 100),
```

## RANKORA CAREER PAGE & JOB LISTING INFRASTRUCTURE - COMPREHENSIVE EXPLORATION REPORT

Based on my thorough exploration of the Rankora codebase, here's the complete picture of what exists for career pages and job listing features:

---

### 1. APPLY PAGE (`src/pages/Apply.tsx`)

**What exists:**
- **Single job apply form** — `/apply/:jobId` route (public, no auth required)
- **Public candidate-facing interface** showing:
  - Job title
  - Job description (displayed in a read-only box)
  - Form fields: Name, Email, Phone, LinkedIn URL (optional)
  - Resume upload (PDF, DOCX, DOC, RTF, TXT; max 10MB)
  - Success/error screens
- **Fetches minimal job data** via `get_job_apply_info` RPC (no auth required)
- **Form validation** + file validation
- **Application submission** via POST to `/functions/v1/submit-application` edge function

**Limitations:**
- Shows **only one job at a time** — no job listing/browsing
- No metadata displayed (location, salary, employment type, department, remote/onsite)
- Header/footer are hardcoded "Rankora" branding, no company customization
- **No career page builder** exists

---

### 2. ROUTES (`src/App.tsx`)

**Public routes:**
- `GET /` → LandingPage (unauthenticated) or Index (authenticated)
- `GET /apply/:jobId` → Apply page (public, no auth)
- `GET /book-demo`, `/request-feature`, `/changelog` → Public marketing pages

**Authenticated routes:**
- `GET /jobs` → Index (protected, shows user's own jobs only)
- `GET /admin` → Admin page (admins only)
- `GET /settings`, `/profile`, `/billing`, `/team`, `/tasks` → Protected

**What's missing:**
- No `/careers` or `/jobs/public` route for browsing all job listings
- No customizable career page route (e.g., `/company/:slug` or `/careers`)
- No public job listing page

---

### 3. JOB DATA FIELDS (`jobs` table schema)

**Current fields in the jobs table:**
- `id` (UUID)
- `user_id` (who created the job)
- `team_id` (optional, links to teams table)
- `title` (text, nullable)
- `job_description` (text, required)
- `status` (pending, processing, completed, failed)
- `must_weight`, `nice_weight`, `optional_weight` (scoring config)
- `jd_analysis_json` (JSONB — parsed must-haves, nice-to-haves, optional)
- `dynamic_weights_json` (JSONB — custom scoring weights per dimension)
- `jd_analysis_prompt` (text)
- `rewritten_jd` (text — AI-rewritten job description)
- `jd_quality_score` (JSONB)
- `inbox_email` (text — email address for forwarding resumes)
- `created_at`, `updated_at`

**What's missing:**
- **No location field** (no location data at all)
- **No salary/compensation fields** (min_salary, max_salary, currency, salary_type)
- **No department field**
- **No employment_type field** (full-time, part-time, contract, temporary, internship)
- **No remote/onsite field** (remote, hybrid, onsite)
- **No job_url field** (custom public URL for the job)
- **No is_public flag** (to control which jobs appear on career page)
- **No description_short** (summary vs. full description)
- **No company_name field** (could use team.name instead)

---

### 4. LANDING PAGE (`src/components/LandingPage.tsx`)

## What We're Building
A branded public career page that recruiters can share. Like Manatal's career page but simpler for MVP.

## Manatal's Features (reference only — we adapt for our stack):
- No-code branded career page per company
- Custom domain support (future)
- Job listings with location, department, type
- Application form with custom fields
- Resume parsing + AI scoring on submit
- Analytics (GA4/GTM)
- API for embedding

## Our Stack
- React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind + shadcn-ui
- Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth + RLS + Edge Functions)
- React Query, React Router 6

## What Already Exists
- `/apply/:jobId` — public apply page per job (name, email, phone, linkedin, resume upload)
- `submit-application` edge function — handles form + file upload
- `applications` table with RLS (public insert, owner select)
- `teams` table with `name` field (company name)
- `jobs` table with: title, job_description, status, created_at, jd_analysis_json
- `get_job_apply_info` RPC — returns job id, title, status, job_description (public, no auth)
- SEO system: seo_settings, seo_pages tables, SeoHead component
- Sitemap edge function

## MVP Career Page Requirements

### 1. Career Page Settings (Admin/Dashboard)
New section in the recruiter dashboard to configure their career page:
- Company name (from teams.name)
- Company logo URL
- Brand color (hex)
- Tagline / hero text
- About section (rich text or plain text)
- Career page URL slug (e.g., `rankora.co/careers/boldteq`)

### 2. Public Career Page (`/careers/:slug`)
Public route (no auth). Shows:
- Company header (logo, name, tagline)
- About section
- List of open jobs (title, location, department, employment type)
- Click job → expand description + "Apply" button
- Apply button → redirects to existing `/apply/:jobId`

### 3. Job Metadata (extend jobs table)
Add optional fields to jobs:
- `location` (text, e.g., "San Francisco, CA" or "Remote")
- `department` (text, e.g., "Engineering", "Marketing")
- `employment_type` (text, e.g., "Full-time", "Part-time", "Contract")
- `is_published` (boolean, default false — controls visibility on career page)
- `salary_range` (text, optional, e.g., "$80k - $120k")

### 4. Career Page Config Table
New table: `career_page_config`
- `team_id` (FK to teams, unique — one config per team)
- `slug` (unique, URL-safe)
- `company_name` (text)
- `logo_url` (text, nullable)
- `brand_color` (text, default '#6366f1')
- `tagline` (text, nullable)
- `about` (text, nullable)
- `is_active` (boolean, default false)
- `created_at`, `updated_at`

### 5. Public RPC for Career Page
Need a SECURITY DEFINER function that returns career page config + published jobs without auth:
```sql
get_career_page(p_slug text)
returns: { config, jobs[] }
```

## Architecture Constraints
- Public route — no auth required
- RLS: career_page_config readable by anyone (for public page), writable by team owner/admin
- Jobs exposed only if `is_published = true` and career page `is_active = true`
- Reuse existing Apply flow — career page just links to `/apply/:jobId`
- Must work with existing SEO infrastructure

1. Complete SQL migration
2. New routes and components
3. Career page settings component (in dashboard)
4. Public career page component
5. Data flow diagram
6. What to add to sidebar

# Plan: Tasks + Team Notifications

## Context
Completing Section 2 of the Rankora roadmap. Team Members + Notes are built. Now adding Tasks (assign work to teammates with due dates) and Team Notifications (stage changes, new notes, task assignments show in notification bell).

---

## Part 1: Tasks

### New Migration: `supabase/migrations/20260407200000_add_tasks_and_team_notifications.sql`

**Tasks table:**
```sql
CREATE TABLE public.tasks (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES teams(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title text NOT NULL,
  description text,
  assigned_to uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  job_id uuid REFERENCES jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  resume_id uuid REFERENCES resumes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo' CHECK (status IN ('todo', 'in_progress', 'done')),
  priority text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium' CHECK (priority IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')),
  due_date date,
  completed_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

**RLS:** Team members can SELECT. Owner/admin/creator can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Assigned user can UPDATE status.

**Extend notifications CHECK constraint:**
```sql
ALTER TABLE notifications DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS notifications_type_check;
ALTER TABLE notifications ADD CONSTRAINT notifications_type_check
  CHECK (type IN ('ranking_complete','ranking_failed','credits_low','credits_added','system',
                  'stage_changed','note_added','task_assigned','task_completed','member_joined'));
```

**DB triggers for auto-notifications:**
- `stage_history` INSERT → notify all team members of that job (except actor)
- `candidate_notes` INSERT → notify team members (except author)
- `tasks` INSERT (when assigned_to is set) → notify assigned user
- `tasks` UPDATE (status='done') → notify task creator

### New Hook: `src/hooks/useTasks.tsx`
- React Query: `["tasks", teamId]`
- CRUD mutations: createTask, updateTask, deleteTask, toggleComplete
- Realtime subscription on tasks table

### New Page: `src/pages/Tasks.tsx`
Using SidebarLayout. Structure from roadmap mockup:
- Header: "My Tasks" + overdue/due-soon badges + "+ New Task" button
- Sections: Overdue (red), Due Soon (amber), Upcoming, Completed (strikethrough)
- Each task row: checkbox + title + assigned avatar + due date badge
- New Task dialog: title, description, assign to (team member select), job link (optional), priority, due date

### Sidebar: Add "Tasks" nav item after "My Jobs"

### Route: `/tasks` in App.tsx

---

## Part 2: Team Notifications

### Extend NotificationBell icon map
Add new entries to `ICON_MAP` in `src/components/NotificationBell.tsx`:
```typescript
stage_changed: { icon: ArrowRight, color: "text-violet-600", bg: "bg-violet-100" },
note_added: { icon: MessageSquare, color: "text-blue-600", bg: "bg-blue-100" },
task_assigned: { icon: CheckSquare, color: "text-orange-600", bg: "bg-orange-100" },
task_completed: { icon: CheckCircle2, color: "text-emerald-600", bg: "bg-emerald-100" },
member_joined: { icon: UserPlus, color: "text-primary", bg: "bg-primary/10" },
```

### Update Notification type in NotificationBell
Expand the `type` union to include new types.

### DB Triggers create notifications automatically
- No frontend code needed for creating notifications — triggers handle it
- Each trigger creates one notification per relevant team member

---

## Files to Create/Modify

| File | Action | What |
|------|--------|------|
| `supabase/migrations/20260407200000_add_tasks_and_team_notifications.sql` | NEW | Tasks table, extend notifications, DB triggers |

| `src/App.tsx` | EDIT | Add /tasks route |
| `src/components/NotificationBell.tsx` | EDIT | Add new notification types + icons |

---

## Verification
1. `npm run build` — zero errors
2. `npx supabase db push` — migrations apply

4. Change candidate stage → team members see notification

content.text: I have completed my thorough audit. Here is the full findings report. --- ## Code Review: Career Page Feature — Deep Audit **Date:** 2025-04-05 **Reviewer:** Sage **Review Mode:** C (Focused Feature Review) **Stack:** A (React + Supabase) **Scope:** Career Page feature — database migration, settings page, public career page, job listing card, apply integration, sidebar nav, routing ### Verdict: PASS WITH WARNINGS ### Summary The Career Page feature is well-structured with solid RLS policies, proper SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, good skeleton loading states, and thoughtful UX (slug auto-generation, debounced availability checking, department filters). However, there are 2 high-severity bugs that will cause runtime failures for users, plus several medium-severity issues around data scoping, security hardening, and validation mismatches between frontend and database. --- ### Issues Found | # | Severity | Category | File | Line(s) | Issue | Required Fix | Effort | |---|----------|----------|------|---------|-------|--------------|--------| | 1 | **HIGH** | Bug | `src/pages/CareerSettings.tsx` | 69 | **3-digit hex accepted by frontend, rejected by DB** — `isValidHex()` accepts `#FFF` (3-digit) but the DB constraint `career_page_brand_color_format` requires exactly 6 digits (`^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$`). A user entering `#FFF` will see "valid" in the UI but get a DB constraint violation on save. | Either: (a) change `isValidHex` to only accept 6-digit hex: `/^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$/.test(value)`, or (b) expand the 3-digit hex to 6-digit before saving (e.g. `#FFF` -> `#FFFFFF`). Option (a) is simpler and more correct. | 10 min | | 2 | **HIGH** | Bug / Data Scope | `src/pages/CareerSettings.tsx` | 203-212 | **Jobs fetched by `user_id`, but career page RPC fetches by `team_id`** — The "Published Jobs" table queries `.eq("user_id", userId)` which only shows the current user's jobs. But the public `get_career_page` RPC fetches `WHERE j.team_id = _config.team_id`. If team member A creates jobs and team member B manages the career page, B will not see A's jobs to toggle them. | Change the query to filter by `team_id` instead of `user_id`: `.eq("team_id", teamId)`. Also update the query key from `["career-jobs", userId]` to `["career-jobs", teamId]`. | 15 min | | 3 | **HIGH** | Security | `supabase/migrations/20260407000000_applications_mvp_fixes.sql` | 9-18 | **`get_job_apply_info` is SECURITY DEFINER without `SET search_path`** — This function uses `SECURITY DEFINER` but does not set `search_path = public`. This is a search_path injection risk. An attacker could potentially create a schema with a malicious `jobs` table. The career page RPC (`get_career_page`) correctly sets `SET search_path = public` but this one does not. | Add `SET search_path = public` to the function definition. Requires a new migration to recreate the function. | 15 min | | 4 | **MEDIUM** | Data Integrity | `supabase/migrations/20260407300000_add_career_page.sql` | 34 | **Slug regex rejects 1-2 character slugs but also rejects exactly 3 chars in edge cases** — The regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9\-]{1,58}[a-z0-9]$` requires minimum 3 characters (start + 1-58 middle + end). This is correct per the comment "3-60 chars". However, the frontend `slugify()` function on line 60-66 does not enforce a minimum length of 3. A company name of "AI" would produce slug "ai" (2 chars), which would fail the DB constraint silently on save. | Add a minimum length check in `handleSave` before the DB call: `if (slug.trim().length < 3) { toast.error("Slug must be at least 3 characters"); return; }`. Also add a visual hint below the slug input. | 10 min | | 5 | **MEDIUM** | Security | `src/pages/CareerPage.tsx` | 133-137 | **`logo_url` rendered as `` without validation** — The `logo_url` is user-provided and rendered directly into an `` tag. While `` tags are not a direct XSS vector (no script execution), the URL could point to a tracking pixel, an intranet resource, or an extremely large image that crashes the page. There is no URL validation on the frontend or backend. | Add URL validation: (a) In `handleSave` in CareerSettings.tsx, validate the URL starts with `https://` or is empty. (b) On the public page, add `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"` to the img tag and consider constraining dimensions. ## Career Page Feature Gap Analysis: Rankora vs. Top ATS Platforms

### Current State of Rankora's Career Page

Rankora currently has a functional but minimal career page implementation:

**What exists today:**
- Public career page at `/careers/:slug` with company branding (name, logo, brand color, tagline, about section)
- Department filter (pill-based, single department at a time)
- Job listing cards showing title, location, department, employment type, salary range, posted date
- "Apply Now" button per job, linking to `/apply/:jobId`
- Application form: name (required), email (required), phone (optional), resume upload (optional, drag-and-drop), LinkedIn URL (optional)
- Application management tab: status tracking (pending/reviewed/shortlisted/rejected), resume download, real-time updates via Supabase subscription
- Career settings page: company name, URL slug (with availability check), logo URL, brand color, tagline, about text, publish toggle, job publish toggles
- "Powered by Rankora" footer
- Slug validation and uniqueness enforcement at DB level

---

### Competitor Feature Breakdown

#### 1. Manatal Career Page

**Source:** [Manatal Career Page Builder](https://www.manatal.com/features/career-page), [Manatal Advanced Career Page Blog](https://www.manatal.com/blog/advanced-career-page)

- Custom domain hosting (e.g., careers.yourcompany.com)
- Multiple theme templates with modern visual designs
- Custom favicon and social media thumbnails (OG images)
- Custom application forms with mandatory/optional fields, dropdowns, open questions
- Job search by keyword
- Filter by city/country, department/organization, industry
- Advanced job-to-post linking (one job to multiple posts for multi-location, or consolidate many jobs into one post)
- Automatic candidate parsing and AI scoring on application
- Google Analytics integration
- Google Tag Manager support
- Conversion tracking (started vs completed applications)
- Career Page API for embedding on external sites
- CMS compatibility (WordPress, Wix, Squarespace)
- SEO-optimized pages with keyword integration
- Multilingual support (create pages in any language)
- No-code builder (no technical skills required)

#### 2. Greenhouse Career Page

**Source:** [Greenhouse Integration Options](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644-Choose-a-careers-page-integration-option), [Greenhouse Job Board Customization](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18996861758363-Customize-your-job-board), [Greenhouse Google for Jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003185526-Job-post-visibility-on-Google-for-Jobs)

- Five integration tiers: hosted board, embedded iFrame, API-driven with hosted apps, API-driven with custom apps, fully custom API
- Job Board API providing JSON for jobs, offices, departments
- Drop-down filters by department, office, and custom fields
- Schema.org JobPosting structured data for Google for Jobs visibility
- Structured job post locations (offices + custom location lists)
- Logo upload and rich-text formatting on job posts
- Custom application questions and fields per job
- Embeddable job board (iFrame widget for external websites)
- WordPress plugin for Greenhouse job boards
- ADA compliance AA+ capability (in full custom tier)
- Tracking pixels and source tracking
- Spam prevention mechanisms
- Available across all subscription tiers (Core, Plus, Pro)

#### 3. Lever Career Page

**Source:** [Lever Job Sites](https://www.lever.co/lever-job-site/), [Lever Career Site Builder](https://www.lever.co/career-site-builder/), [Lever HTML Widget](https://help.lever.co/hc/en-us/articles/20087269502237-Career-Site-Builder-HTML-widget)

- Career Site Builder (paid add-on) with drag-and-drop editor
- Site Theme panel: customize text, buttons, images, backgrounds, navigation across entire site
- Widget library: social sharing buttons, multimedia, contact forms, HTML/CSS embeds
- "Keep in Touch" form for general interest candidates (talent pool collection)
- Google Analytics integration for traffic and engagement tracking
- Internal vs external candidate pathways (separate experiences)
- Custom branding: fonts, colors, imagery
- Schema.org structured data and OG/Twitter Card metadata
- Custom HTML widget for embedding third-party content (videos, forms)
- Responsive design (mobile-optimized)
- SEO metadata (page-level)
- New Relic browser monitoring
- Employee referral programs and internal mobility support

#### 4. Workable Career Page

**Source:** [Workable Careers Pages](https://www.workable.com/features/careers-pages), [Workable Careers Page Builder](https://help.workable.com/hc/en-us/articles/360052322194-Managing-the-Careers-page-site-builder), [Workable Job Widget](https://help.workable.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012801727-How-to-embed-jobs-on-your-website-job-widget)

- Drag-and-drop page builder with templated sections:
  - Header and Footer (required)
  - List of Jobs (required, with optional search)
  - Image with Text
  - Paragraph
  - Testimonials (employee photos + quotes)
  - Image Gallery
  - Departments (dynamic, auto-updates)
  - Locations (office addresses)
  - Benefits (tile-based with icons)
  - Video (YouTube/Vimeo embed)
  - Numbers (key company figures)
  - Social Media links (Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube)
- Job search bar (requires minimum 6 published jobs)
- Department filtering
- Talent Pool: general applications when no suitable job is found
- Google Analytics and tracking pixel integration
- Auto-source tracking for candidates
- Embeddable job widget (JavaScript snippet) with CSS/JS customization hooks
- Widget displays jobs by location or department
- WordPress plugin for embedding
- Custom domain hosting (via account manager)
- Mobile-responsive design
- Invite team members to edit (non-technical editor access)
- Undo/redo in editing sessions
- Social sharing buttons (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn)
- GDPR/EEO compliance info auto-included in footer
- Multilingual page support

#### 5. BambooHR Career Page

**Source:** [BambooHR ATS](https://www.bamboohr.com/platform/applicant-tracking-system/), [BambooHR Review](https://juicebox.ai/blog/bamboohr-reviews)

- Basic career page with minimal customization (weakest of the five)
- Job posting creation and distribution to free boards (Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter)
- Social media channel posting
- Custom job descriptions with qualifications and branding
- Customizable offer letter templates with auto-populated candidate details
- E-signatures for offer acceptance
- Mobile app support
- No advanced page builder (generic page, limited branding)
- No dynamic content, video testimonials, or section-based builder
- Integration with external job boards and sourcing tools via marketplace
